items.title: SCAD ALIGN trial secures US funding to investigate optimal treatment for spontaneous coronary dissection
items.summary: The Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai (New York, USA) has received a US$2 million grant from the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI), part of the National Institutes of Health (NIH), to study which therapy is optimal for treating spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD).

items.title: AMA assigns new CPT codes for renal denervation
items.summary: The American Medical Association (AMA) has approved two new category I current procedural terminology (CPT) codes describing renal denervation.

items.title: Size adjustable pulmonary valve gains US FDA approval
items.summary: Edwards Lifesciences has announced that the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved the Autus size-adjustable valve, a surgical pulmonary valve designed specifically for paediatric patients with congenital heart disease who require pulmonary valve replacement.

items.title: No net benefit for no-touch graft harvesting technique at seven years
items.summary: Seven-year follow-up data from the SWEDEGRAFT trial, testing the ‘no-touch’ technique for graft harvesting for coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery, do not establish a net clinical benefit for the routine use of the technique, investigators say.

items.title: Medtronic announces regulatory milestones for newest cardiac mapping and ablation software
items.summary: Medtronic today announced regulatory milestones for software used with two cardiac ablation platforms, including US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) clearance and a CE mark for the latest Affera Prism-2 mapping software.

items.title: Hybrid endoscopic imaging system gets expanded indication for cardiac surgery procedures
items.summary: Karl Storz has announced that the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has cleared expanded indications for the TIPCAM1 Rubina video endoscope for use in selected cardiac surgical procedures.

items.title: Medtech incubator backs novel transcatheter implant for functional mitral regurgitation
items.summary: Mitria Medical, an early-stage, structural heart company developing a next-generation transcatheter solution for mitral valve repair, has announced a partnership with T45 Labs, a Silicon Valley medtech incubator focused on minimally invasive cardiovascular technologies.

items.title: FastWave shares interim results for Sola L-IVL system
items.summary: FastWave Medical has announced interim results from the first-in-human (FIH) feasibility study of its Sola laser intravascular lithotripsy (L-IVL) system for treating calcified coronary artery disease. Thirty patients were treated at two clinical sites.

items.title: AI, ablation innovation and multidisciplinary education to take centre stage at 2026 Heart Rhythm Congress
items.summary: The 2026 Heart Rhythm Congress (HRC; 11–13 October, Birmingham, UK) is set to bring the international heart rhythm community—clinicians, researchers, allied health professionals, patients and industry—together once again, focusing on artificial intelligence (AI), the future of cardiac ablation, and more.

items.title: Innovative tricuspid TEER system wins TCT Plus Middle East Shark Tank competition
items.summary: Startric, the developer of a next-generation transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) system for the treatment of tricuspid heart valve disease, has been named as the winner of the Shark Tank cardiovascular innovation competition at the 2026 TCT Plus Middle East conference (17–19 September, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia).

items.title: AI software for detecting undiagnosed MR gains US FDA approval
items.summary: Tempus AI has received 510(k) clearance from the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for Tempus ECG-MR, an AI product that analyses standard 12-lead resting electrocardiograms (ECGs) to detect signs associated with undiagnosed moderate or severe mitral regurgitation (MR).

items.title: Delays in receiving TAVI linked to higher risk of heart failure hospitalisation or mortality
items.summary: Prolonged delays in receiving transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) after a diagnosis of severe aortic stenosis (AS) may be associated with a higher risk of hospitalisation for heart failure or all-cause mortality, a real-world, single-centre study from Japan has found.

items.title: ECG case series for paramedics: October 2026
items.summary: Journal of Paramedic Practice, Volume 18, Issue 10, Page 403-403, October 2026.…

items.title: StopAfib.org announces recipient of 2026 Eric N Prystowsky Advocate for Patients Award
items.summary: At its recent annual patient conference (7–9 August, Dallas, USA), StopAfib.org bestowed its prestigious Eric N Prystowsky Advocate for Patients Award on Jonathan Piccini (Duke University, Durham, USA) to recognise his “outstanding commitment” to atrial fibrillation (AF) patients and their families.

items.title: STAR Apollo mapping technology demonstrates 90% freedom from AF at one year following redo ablations
items.summary: Rhythm AI has announced results from the STAR Apollo study evaluating the company’s Stochastic Trajectory Analysis of Ranked signals (STAR) mapping approach in redo ablation procedures of patients with persistent atrial fibrillation (AF).

items.title: Current approach to detecting and treating hypertension is not working, say researchers
items.summary: The current approach to detecting and treating hypertension is ‘not fit for purpose’ say researchers who found high levels of undiagnosed and uncontrolled disease across the country.

items.title: da Vinci 5 gains CE mark for adult cardiac surgery in Europe
items.summary: Intuitive says da Vinci 5 received CE mark for adult cardiac surgery in Europe, including coronary artery bypass.

items.title: SELUTION DeNovo subanalysis hints at benefit for balloon-based strategy in high bleeding risk patients
items.summary: Results of a subanalysis of the SELUTION DeNovo trial point towards a potential clinical benefit of a drug-eluting balloon (DEB)-based percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) strategy in patients at high bleeding risk.

items.title: iPerf concludes clinical trial of novel dual-lumen femoral arterial cannula for cardiopulmonary support
items.summary: iPerf has announced the conclusion of its first clinical trial evaluating its dual-lumen femoral arterial cannula for cardiopulmonary support.

items.title: Meta-analysis highlights uncertainties over clinical benefit of LAAC compared to oral anticoagulation
items.summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis of eight trials comparing left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) to oral anticoagulation in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) has shown similar rates of stroke and major bleeding between the two approaches, but the catheter-based treatment was linked to a higher risk of…

items.title: Meta-analysis highlights uncertainties over clinical benefit of LAAC compared to oral anticoagulation
items.summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis of eight trials comparing left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) to oral anticoagulation in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) has shown similar rates of stroke and major bleeding between the two approaches, but the catheter-based treatment was linked to a higher risk of…

items.title: Valve surgery study aims to link randomised trial with real-world data
items.summary: Researchers at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai (New York, USA) have received a US$3.6 million, four-year grant from the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI), part of the National Institutes of Health (NIH), to develop an approach to extend evidence from clinical trials to a broader population…

items.title: Heart failure nurses' experiences of providing palliative care for people with heart failure
items.summary: International Journal of Palliative Nursing, Volume 32, Issue 9, Page 430-441, September 2026.

items.title: Corcym expands mitral repair platform with first-on-human use of Memo 4D Curve annuloplasty system
items.summary: Corcym has announced the first-in-human implant of Memo 4D Curve, a semi-rigid open-configuration annuloplasty ring for mitral valve repair. The procedure, a robotic cardiac surgery, was performed by Michael Ibrahim at UVA Health University Medical Center (Charlottesville, USA).

items.title: CMS updates coverage determination for TAVI
items.summary: The US Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) has updated its national coverage determination (NCD) for transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), which, amongst other changes, now includes coverage for the treatment of asymptomatic severe aortic stenosis (AS).

items.title: Da Vinci 5 surgical system CE marked for adult cardiac surgery
items.summary: Intuitive has announced that its da Vinci 5 surgical system has received CE mark approval for adult cardiac surgery in Europe, including thoracoscopically-assisted cardiotomy procedures and minimally invasive coronary artery bypass procedures.

items.title: HighLife to advance its TMVR clinical development programme
items.summary: HighLife SAS has announced the successful completion of a financing round worth in excess of US$90 million, with funding to be used to accelerate its commercial expansion across Europe and advance its US clinical development programme.

items.title: Mölnlycke launches Biogel radiation protection gloves to reduce clinician hand exposure during procedures
items.summary: Mölnlycke Health Care US announced today the launch of a new surgical glove range designed to reduce clinician hand exposure to scattered radiation during fluoroscopy-guided, interventional and other image-dependent procedures.

items.title: Selution SLR gains US FDA approval for coronary ISR
items.summary: Cordis has announced that the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved the Selution SLR (sustained limus release) drug-eluting balloon (DEB) for the treatment of coronary in-stent restenosis (ISR).

items.title: Texray appoints Ziv Haskal to advisory board
items.summary: Texray has announced that interventional radiologist Ziv J Haskal (University of Virginia School of Medicine, Charlottesville, USA) has joined the company’s clinical and scientific advisory board.

items.title: First-in-human Field PULSE trial demonstrates 94.2% per-vein PVI durability rate with optimised PFA waveform
items.summary: Field Medical has announced the publication of 12-month results from its first-in-human Field PULSE trial in JACC: Clinical Electrophysiology alongside their simultaneous presentation as a late-breaking clinical trial at HRX Live 2026 (18–20 September, Atlanta, USA).

items.title: NeuroPulse study reports substantial reduction in recurrent AF events via non-invasive neuromodulation after ablation
items.summary: StimCardio Medical has announced positive results from the randomised, double-blind, sham-controlled NeuroPulse pilot study evaluating non-invasive median nerve stimulation (MNS) following atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation.

items.title: Abbott secures US FDA approval for Aveir VR Mini ventricular leadless pacemaker
items.summary: Abbott announced this week that the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved its Aveir VR Mini ventricular leadless pacemaker (LP)—the latest-generation ventricular device in Abbott’s Aveir leadless pacing platform.

items.title: Luma Vision secures US FDA clearance to expand capabilities of Verafeye platform
items.summary: Luma Vision has announced US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) clearance expanding the capabilities of Verafeye, its procedural intelligence platform.

items.title: Pulmonary artery denervation shows promise in pulmonary hypertension linked to heart-failure
items.summary: Patients with pulmonary hypertension associated with heart failure were less likely to experience clinical worsening when treated with transcatheter pulmonary artery denervation (PADN) compared to receiving medical therapy alone, the results of a randomised trial conducted at 25 sites in China have shown.

items.title: Percutaneous insertion of a cerebral protection device during TAVI for preventing stroke
items.summary: HealthTech guidance — Draft guidance. Closes 06/10/2026.

items.title: Abbott receives US FDA approval to treat challenging AF cases with TactiFlex Duo ablation catheter
items.summary: Abbott has announced it has received US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval to treat patients with challenging cases of atrial fibrillation (AF) using its sensor-enabled TactiFlex Duo ablation catheter.

items.title: Trust backpedals after cardiology department told GPs it could not convert A&G to referrals
items.summary: Exclusive A hospital trust has said a message telling GPs it was unable to convert advice and guidance (A&G) requests to referrals had been sent ‘in error’.

items.title: Implicity secures US$40 million in growth equity funding to scale AI-driven cardiac monitoring platform
items.summary: Implicity has secured a US$40 million funding round led by European tech growth capital firm IRIS alongside Five Arrows, the alternative assets arm of Rothschild & Co.

items.title: DynamX coronary bioadaptor gains approval from Japanese MHLW
items.summary: Elixir Medical has announced that Japan’s Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW) has approved the DynamX coronary bioadaptor system for the treatment of coronary artery disease. The approval establishes bioadaptor as a new medical device category in Japan, Elixir says in a press release.

items.title: ESC 2026: DOACs only prevent leaflet thickening in the short term after TAVI
items.summary: Three months of direct oral anticoagulation (DOAC) therapy was successful in reducing hypoattenuated leaflet thickening (HALT) in patients who had undergone transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), but the effect diminished nine months after the discontinuation of the therapy.

items.title: CaRi-Heart for predicting cardiac risk in adults with suspected coronary artery disease (CAD)
items.summary: HealthTech guidance — Draft guidance. Closes 05/10/2026.

items.title: PREMIUM trial results not supportive of prasugrel monotherapy at the time of PCI for STEMI
items.summary: Low-dose prasugrel monotherapy failed to show non-inferiority when compared to 12 months of dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) against a composite endpoint of all-cause death, stroke or myocardial infarction (MI) in ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) patients undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention…

items.title: Shark Tank cardiovascular innovation competition comes to the Middle East
items.summary: A shortlist of four finalists has been named for the TCT Plus Middle East Shark Tank cardiovascular innovation competition, with a winner to be selected at the second edition of the conference taking place this week (17–19 September, Riyadh, Saudi Arabia).

items.title: IMDS launches microcatheter designed to improve lesion crossing in challenging anatomy
items.summary: Interventional Medical Device Solutions (IMDS) has announced the US launch of NHanceIT, an over-the-wire, single-lumen microcatheter designed to improve lesion crossing in challenging coronary anatomy.

items.title: LightningWire transseptal puncture system used in first clinical cases
items.summary: ElectroWire Medical has announced the completion of the first clinical cases with its US Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-cleared LightningWire transseptal puncture system at Spartanburg Medical Center in Spartanburg, USA.

items.title: LightningWire transseptal puncture system used in first clinical cases
items.summary: ElectroWire Medical has announced the completion of the first clinical cases with its US Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-cleared LightningWire transseptal puncture system at Spartanburg Medical Center in Spartanburg, USA.

items.title: Emboliner embolic protection device gains US FDA clearance
items.summary: Emboline has announced that the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has granted 510(k) clearance for the Emboliner embolic protection system for use during transcatheter heart procedures.

items.title: Cardiovascular disease linked to higher risk of cancer death
items.summary: People with cardiovascular disease are more likely to develop cancer and die from the disease than those without cardiovascular conditions, a new study has found. Researchers from the universities of Aberdeen and Keele analysed data from 22,534 people over more than 25 years.

items.title: First-in-human implant for TriMemo tricuspid annuloplasty technology
items.summary: Corcym has announced the first-in-human implantation of TriMemo, a semi-rigid annuloplasty ring dedicated to tricuspid valve repair.

items.title: GPs must not prescribe semaglutide for CVD risk without ‘written confirmation’ of funding
items.summary: GP practices and LMCs should ask for ‘written confirmation’ of commissioning from ICBs before prescribing semaglutide for cardiovascular risk reduction, the BMA has advised.

items.title: First US patient treated with Saturn TMVR system
items.summary: InnovHeart has announced the successful implantation of the first US patient with the Saturn transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) system as part of the CASSINI-US early feasibility study.

items.title: Early statin use linked to lower dementia risk in type 2 diabetes
items.summary: Early use of statins after a type 2 diabetes diagnosis could reduce the risk of developing dementia, new research suggests. Researchers at Copenhagen University Hospital analysed Danish health records for 132,585 people with type 2 diabetes, comparing dementia rates according to when they began statin treatment.

items.title: Medtronic’s Endurant stent graft system receives CE mark for updated rupture labelling
items.summary: Medtronic has received CE-mark approval for the Endurant stent graft system to remove a ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm (rAAA) treatment warning, the company shared in a press release this week. The labelling update follows the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) labelling approval received in October 2025.

items.title: Abbott’s TactiFlex Duo ablation catheter achieves positive outcomes in complex AF cases
items.summary: Abbott has announced late-breaking, 12-month data from the global FlexPulse investigational device exemption (IDE) study that show favourable safety and effectiveness outcomes for its investigational, sensor-enabled TactiFlex Duo ablation catheter to treat patients with challenging cases of atrial fibrillation (AF).

items.title: ESC 2026: wearable monitor improves diagnosis of heart rhythm disorders after fainting
items.summary: Early electrocardiogram (ECG) monitoring initiated in the emergency department (ED) has the potential to transform the care of thousands of patients who attend the ED with unexplained fainting.

items.title: ESC 2026: edoxaban fails to reduce stroke or systemic embolism in unselected patients with post-ICH atrial fibrillation
items.summary: Edoxaban—an oral anticoagulant medication—failed to reduce stroke or systemic embolism but did increase major bleeding in high-risk patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) who had experienced an intracranial haemorrhage (ICH) within the ENRICH-AF trial, from which results were presented for the first time at the 2026…

items.title: ESC 2026: ICDs may benefit certain younger patients with mild-to-moderate heart dysfunction
items.summary: While younger patients appeared to benefit, implantable cardioverter-defibrillators (ICDs) did not improve the primary endpoint overall in the CMR GUIDE trial, according to new data presented at the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) congress (28–31 August, Munich, Germany) and published simultaneously in the…

items.title: ESC 2026: targeted lead placement is no better than standard placement in CRT
items.summary: Targeted placement of a left ventricular lead does not improve outcomes in patients with heart failure undergoing cardiac resynchronisation therapy (CRT), according to results presented at the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) congress (28–31 August, Munich, Germany) and published simultaneously in The Lancet.

items.title: AI cardiovascular diagnostic specialist Elucid completes latest financing round
items.summary: Elucid has raised US$55 million in an oversubscribed series D financing, with the funding to support the commercialisation of its artificial intelligence (AI)-powered cardiovascular imaging platform.

items.title: ESC 2026: catheter ablation does not appear to improve quality of life related to AF
items.summary: Catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation (AF) did not significantly improve AF-related quality of life compared with a sham procedure, despite reducing AF recurrence, as per the main findings of the PVI-SHAM-AF trial presented at the 2026 European Society of Cardiology (ESC) congress (28–31 August, Munich, Germany)…

items.title: ESC 2026: Clopidogrel monotherapy non-inferior to extended DAPT in patients at high ischaemic risk
items.summary: Clopidogrel monotherapy was shown to be non-inferior to extended dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) with clopidogrel and aspirin for net adverse clinical events at 24 months among patients at high risk for ischaemic events after implantation of a drug-eluting stent, results of the A-CLOSE trial presented at the European…

items.title: ESC 2026: trial results do not support routine LAA closure in all patients undergoing planned cardiac surgery
items.summary: Routine concomitant closure of the left atrial appendage (LAA) during open-heart surgery should not be considered unless patients are high risk for stroke, results of the LAACS-2 trial, presented at the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) congress (28–31 August, Munich, Germany), have shown.

items.title: ESC 2026: Trial results do not support routine LAA closure in all patients undergoing planned cardiac surgery
items.summary: Routine concomitant closure of the left atrial appendage (LAA) during open-heart surgery should not be considered unless patients are high risk for stroke, results of the LAAACS-2 trial, presented at the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) 2026 congress (28–31 August, Munich, Germany), have shown.
